key_insight: AnimationBench provides the first flexible, character-centric benchmark tailored to animation-style video generation, enabling rigorous evaluation of stylized appearance, exaggerated motion, and character consistency across open-domain content.
problem_solved: Existing video benchmarks are built for realistic videos and use fixed prompts and rigid pipelines, making them unsuitable for assessing animation-specific challenges like stylization, expressive motion, and character-centric continuity.
method: Curate an animation-focused evaluation corpus and flexible prompt sets that cover diverse styles, characters, and exaggerated motions.
Introduce character-centric metrics and evaluation protocols (e.g., identity/pose consistency, stylization fidelity, motion exaggeration) designed for animated content.
Provide an open, modular toolkit that supports custom prompts, automated scoring, and human-in-the-loop assessment for open-domain and application-specific evaluation.
impact: AnimationBench fills a critical evaluation gap, giving researchers and practitioners a standardized, animation-aware way to compare and improve video generation models and to better align metrics with perceptual quality for character-driven animation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison panel: ground-truth vs. model outputs highlighting stylization and motion differences
Pipeline diagram: dataset → prompt variations → automated metrics + human evaluation → aggregate score
Radar chart: multi-metric model performance (identity consistency, motion realism, stylization fidelity, temporal coherence)
Character-tracking overlay: visualizing identity/pose consistency across frames
paper_title: AnimationBench: Are Video Models Good at Character-Centric Animation?
paper_authors: Leyi Wu, Pengjun Fang, Kai Sun, Yazhou Xing, Yinwei Wu
